correctness.rationale: The forbidden-induced-subgraph equivalence is proved for every finite nonempty graph of maximum degree at most two. Each path factor follows from an exact binary-run count including n=1,2; each cycle factor includes the necessary C3 exception and a cyclic-boundary count valid for n>=4. The truncated product counts each admissible global two-coloring exactly once. The three-odd-cycle argument is a pigeonhole lower bound with matching constructive two-class colorings, and proper three-colorability gives a uniform upper bound. Independent brute-force forbidden-four-set checks passed on 26 single-component families and 134 disconnected cases; finite computations are corroborative, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The complete two-color enumeration over all degree-two graphs is a natural class-wide exact invariant of the recently investigated threshold-partition problem. The four-state product records a nonlocal induced-2K2 interaction between components, and the exact three-odd-cycle cutoff shows a sharp, interpretable partition-number transition on the canonical sparse class. The result is more substantial than a trivial chromatic bound or a small enumeration table.
